nahhas-irab:1-1.t: The original form, according to Sībawayh, is أناس, and the alif and lām [of الناس] are a replacement for the hamza.

nahhas-irab:2-2.t: A naʿt (adjective). One says: ملك بيّن المُلك (a king with evident kingship), and مالك بيّن المِلك والمُلك (an owner with evident ownership and kingship).

nahhas-irab:4-4.t:
مِنْ شَرِّ الْوَسْواسِ: it is the one who whispers into the breasts, as al-Aʿshā said: [al-Basīṭ] 600-
تسمع للحلي وسواسا إذا انصرفت ... كما استعان بريح عشرق زجل
(You hear a jingling (وسواس) from her ornaments when she turns away, like the rustling of the ʿishriq plant calling on the wind for help.)
الْخَنَّاسِ: from Ibn ʿAbbās there are two narrations. One of them is that he whispers and crouches upon a person's breast, and when Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, is mentioned, he slinks back (يخنس). The other narration is that he whispers, and when he is obeyed he withdraws (انخنس). The two views agree.

nahhas-irab:5-5.t: In the position of the genitive (khafḍ) as a naʿt (adjective); and the nominative is permissible by implying a mubtadaʾ (subject).

nahhas-irab:6-6.t:
One says: جنّيّ, جنّ and جنّة; the hāʾ is for the feminine of the collective, like حجار and حجارة. Abū Jaʿfar said: I asked ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān about His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, وَالنَّاسِ: how are they conjoined to الْجِنَّةِ when they do not whisper? He said: They are maʿṭūf (conjoined) to الوسواس, and the implied order is: "Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind from the evil of the whisperer and of mankind (من شرّ الوسواس والناس)." What he said is good, because placing earlier and later with the wāw is permissible, good and frequent, as [the poet] said: [al-Ṭawīl] 601-
جمعت وفحشا غيبة ونميمة ... ثلاث خصال لست عنها بمرعوي
(You have combined — along with obscenity — backbiting and talebearing: three traits from which you do not desist.)
And Ḥassān said «2»: [al-Ṭawīl] 602-
وما زال في الإسلام من آل هاشم ... دعائم غرّ ما ترام ومفخر
وهم جبل الإسلام والنّاس حولهم ... رضام إلى طود يروق ويقهر
بهاليل منهم جعفر وابن أمّه ... عليّ ومنهم أحمد المتخيّر
(There have never ceased to be in Islam, from the family of Hāshim, illustrious pillars that cannot be reached, and a source of pride; they are the mountain of Islam, and the people around them are boulders beside a lofty peak that excels and overpowers; noble chiefs: among them Jaʿfar and his mother's son ʿAlī, and among them Aḥmad the chosen one.)
So he began the wording with Jaʿfar, then brought ʿAlī after him, then brought the Prophet ﷺ after him, though he is the foremost in reality. «[Translator's note: «2» is a footnote marker in the source whose footnote text is not included here.]»
